gene_protein_organism.gene: aq_1744 / gpmA label in current deposition
gene_protein_organism.protein: histidine-family phosphatase HFP, PP17; UniProt O67630; PDB 9MMH
gene_protein_organism.organism: Aquifex aeolicus; produced in E. coli

case.starting_question: Which phosphatase can complete riboflavin synthesis without destroying pathway inputs, and does an apparent extra isomerase activity belong to it?

actual_observations.result: Two of 22 screened proteins supported a staged ARAPDP-dephosphorylation readout; only HFP supported the full one-pot pathway. IMP depleted NADPH and Ru5P.
HFP preparations also isomerized Ru5P/R5P. Extensive purification and 90 C heating slowed but did not eliminate this activity.
Four of five randomly chosen other preparations also isomerized the sugar. MS detected E. coli RpiA, defeating attribution of isomerase activity to HFP.
HFP also hydrolyzed FMN; substrate instability prevented comparative ARAPDP kinetics.

case.annotation_consequence: HFP is an ARAPDP-phosphatase candidate compatible with the reconstituted pathway, not a demonstrated bifunctional ribose-phosphate isomerase. Native essentiality and exclusivity are not established by this paper.
case.experiment_dependence: Published coupled-pathway reconstitution, NMR, orthogonal purification, contaminant MS and structures. No native knockout/flux experiment is reported.
case.reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: The false extra-activity explanation is explicitly reported. Bounded native-role wording is my assessment rather than adoption of the title essential.
case.verification_scope: Primary relevant complete results/discussion and reconstitution/NMR/purification methods inspected. Supplement MS identification accepted as reported; its underlying spectra were not reanalyzed. Current PDB polymer records bind HFP to aq_1744/O67630; gpmA is a record label, not independent mutase evidence.
